questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Area of a Triangle Given Its Vertices
questions.problem: Calculate the area of the $△\,NPQ$, if $N(1,0,1)$, $P(2,2,3)$, $Q(2,1,1).$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find the vectors $\overset{\to }{NP}$ and $\overset{\to }{NQ}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{NP} & =p-n \\  & =(2i+2j+3k)-(i+k) \\  & =i+2j+2k \\  & =⟨1,2,2⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{NQ} & =q-n \\  & =(2i+j+k)-(i+k) \\  & =i+j \\  & =⟨1,1,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using the formula to compute the cross product, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{NP}\times \overset{\to }{NQ} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 2 & 2 \\ 1 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}|i-|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}|j+|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|k \\  & =(2\cdot 0-1\cdot 2)i-(1\cdot 0-1\cdot 2)j+(1\cdot 1-1\cdot 2)k \\  & =-2i+2j-k \\  & =⟨-2,2,-1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of the parallelogram spanned by $\overset{\to }{NP}$ and $\overset{\to }{NQ}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =|\overset{\to }{NP}\times \overset{\to }{NQ}| \\  & =\sqrt{(-2)^{2}+{2}^{2}+(-1)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{9} \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the area of the triangle is half of the area of the respective parallelogram. So, the area of $△\,NPQ$ is

$$
{A}_{△}=\frac{1}{2}A=\frac{3}{2}.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Altitude of a Triangle Given Its Vertices
questions.problem: Calculate the length of the altitude $ZH$ of the $△\,WYZ$, if $W(2,3,2)$, $Y(1,2,1)$, $Z(1,-1,1).$
questions.worked_solution:
Note that the length of the altitude $ZH$ can be related to the area of $△\,WYZ$ as follows:

$$
{A}_{△}=\frac{1}{2}ZH\cdot WY
$$

So, to find $ZH,$ we first find ${A}_{△}.$ To start, we find the vectors $\overset{\to }{WY}$ and $\overset{\to }{WZ}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{WY} & =y-w \\  & =(i+2j+k)-(2i+3j+2k) \\  & =-i-j-k \\  & =⟨-1,-1,-1⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{WZ} & =z-w \\  & =(i-j+k)-(2i+3j+2k) \\  & =-i-4j-k \\  & =⟨-1,-4,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{WY}\times \overset{\to }{WZ} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ -1 & -1 & -1 \\ -1 & -4 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 \\ -4 & -1\end{aligned}|i-|\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}|j+|\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 \\ -1 & -4\end{aligned}|k \\  & =((-1)\cdot (-1)-(-4)\cdot (-1))i-((-1)\cdot (-1)-(-1)\cdot (-1))j+((-1)\cdot (-4)-(-1)\cdot (-1))k \\  & =-3i+3k \\  & =⟨-3,0,3⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of the parallelogram spanned by $\overset{\to }{WY}$ and $\overset{\to }{WZ}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =|\overset{\to }{WY}\times \overset{\to }{WZ}| \\  & =\sqrt{(-3)^{2}+{0}^{2}+{3}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{18} \\  & =3\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

The area of the triangle is half of the area of the respective parallelogram. So, the area of $△\,WYZ$ is

$$
{A}_{△}=\frac{1}{2}A=\frac{3\sqrt{2}}{2}.
$$

Let's also compute $WY$ since it appears in the formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}WY & =|\overset{\to }{WY}| \\  & =\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+(-1)^{2}+(-1)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, using the formula ${A}_{△}=\frac{1}{2}ZH\cdot WY,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{△} & =\frac{1}{2}ZH\cdot WY \\ \frac{3\sqrt{2}}{2} & =\frac{1}{2}ZH\cdot \sqrt{3} \\ 3\sqrt{2} & =ZH\cdot \sqrt{3} \\ ZH & =\frac{3\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{3}} \\ ZH & =\sqrt{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Calculate the area of the $△\,WXY,$ if $W(3,9,4),$ $X(1,7,3),$ $Y(6,12,8).$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find the vectors $\overset{\to }{WX}$ and $\overset{\to }{WY}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{WX} & =x-w \\  & =(i+7j+3k)-(3i+9j+4k) \\  & =-2i-2j-k \\  & =⟨-2,-2,-1⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{WY} & =y-w \\  & =(6i+12j+8k)-(3i+9j+4k) \\  & =3i+3j+4k \\  & =⟨3,3,4⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using the formula to compute the cross product, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{WX}\times \overset{\to }{WY} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ -2 & -2 & -1 \\ 3 & 3 & 4\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}-2 & -1 \\ 3 & 4\end{aligned}|i-|\begin{aligned}-2 & -1 \\ 3 & 4\end{aligned}|j+|\begin{aligned}-2 & -2 \\ 3 & 3\end{aligned}|k \\  & =((-2)\cdot 4-3\cdot (-1))i-((-2)\cdot 4-3\cdot (-1))j+((-2)\cdot 3-3\cdot (-2))k \\  & =-5i+5j \\  & =⟨-5,5,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of the parallelogram spanned by $\overset{\to }{WX}$ and $\overset{\to }{WY}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =|\overset{\to }{WX}\times \overset{\to }{WY}| \\  & =\sqrt{(-5)^{2}+{5}^{2}+{0}^{2}} \\  & =5\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the area of the triangle is half of the area of the respective parallelogram. So, the area of $△\,WXY$ is

$$
{A}_{△}=\frac{1}{2}A=\frac{5\sqrt{2}}{2}.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Altitude of a Triangle Given Its Vertices
questions.problem: Calculate the length of the altitude $RH$ of the $△\,PRQ,$ if $P(3,0,4),$ $Q(2,3,1),$ $R(0,3,1).$
questions.worked_solution:
Note that the length of the altitude $RH$ can be related to the area of $△\,PQR$ as follows:

$$
{A}_{△}=\frac{1}{2}RH\cdot PQ
$$

So, to find $RH,$ we first find ${A}_{△}.$ To start, we find the vectors $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ and $\overset{\to }{PR}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =q-p \\  & =(2i+3j+k)-(3i+4k) \\  & =-i+3j-3j \\  & =⟨-1,3,-3⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{PR} & =r-p \\  & =(3j+k)-(3i+4k) \\  & =-3i+3j-3k \\  & =⟨-3,3,-3⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ}\times \overset{\to }{PR} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ -1 & 3 & -3 \\ -3 & 3 & -3\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}3 & -3 \\ 3 & -3\end{aligned}|i-|\begin{aligned}-1 & -3 \\ -3 & -3\end{aligned}|j+|\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 \\ -3 & 3\end{aligned}|k \\  & =(3\cdot (-3)-3\cdot (-3))i-((-1)\cdot (-3)-(-3)\cdot (-3))j+((-1)\cdot 3-(-3)\cdot 3)k \\  & =6j+6k \\  & =⟨0,6,6⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of the parallelogram spanned by $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ and $\overset{\to }{PR}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =|\overset{\to }{PQ}\times \overset{\to }{PR}| \\  & =\sqrt{{0}^{2}+{6}^{2}+{6}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{72} \\  & =6\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

The area of the triangle is half of the area of the respective parallelogram. So, the area of $△\,PQR$ is

$$
{A}_{△}=\frac{1}{2}A=\frac{6\sqrt{2}}{2}=3\sqrt{2}.
$$

Let's also compute $PQ$ since it appears in the formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}PQ & =|\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+{3}^{2}+(-3)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{19}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, using the formula ${A}_{△}=\frac{1}{2}RH\cdot PQ,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{△} & =\frac{1}{2}RH\cdot PQ \\ 3\sqrt{2} & =\frac{1}{2}RH\cdot \sqrt{19} \\ 6\sqrt{2} & =RH\cdot \sqrt{19} \\ RH & =\frac{6\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{19}} \\ RH & =\frac{6\sqrt{38}}{19}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Area of a Triangle Given Its Vertices
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find the vectors $\overset{\to }{AB}$ and $\overset{\to }{AC}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =b-a \\  & =(-3i+3j-4k)-(-2i-k) \\  & =-i+3j-3k \\  & =⟨-1,3,-3⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AC} & =c-a \\  & =(-2j+2k)-(-2i-k) \\  & =2i-2j+3k \\  & =⟨2,-2,3⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using the formula to compute the cross product, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB}\times \overset{\to }{AC} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ -1 & 3 & -3 \\ 2 & -2 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}3 & -3 \\ -2 & 3\end{aligned}|i-|\begin{aligned}-1 & -3 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}|j+|\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 \\ 2 & -2\end{aligned}|k \\  & =(3\cdot 3-(-2)\cdot (-3))i-((-1)\cdot 3-2\cdot (-3))j+((-1)\cdot (-2)-2\cdot 3)k \\  & =3i-3j-4k \\  & =⟨3,-3,-4⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of the parallelogram spanned by $\overset{\to }{AB}$ and $\overset{\to }{AC}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =|\overset{\to }{AB}\times \overset{\to }{AC}| \\  & =\sqrt{{3}^{2}+(-3)^{2}+(-4)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{34}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the area of the triangle is half of the area of the respective parallelogram. So, the area of $△\,ABC$ is

$$
{A}_{△}=\frac{1}{2}A=\frac{\sqrt{34}}{2}.
$$
